title: Dense Prime Rectangular Solve
objective: Eliminate scalar host extraction after rectangular dense GF(p) solve_right by using one source-transparent packed typed-Python kernel, with Sage-compatible semantics and benchmarked fallback/native behavior

oracles: Sage solve_right semantics over GF(2), GF(7), and GF(97)

handoff.summary: Rectangular and rank-deficient packed GF(p) solve_right now keeps the existing FLINT/FFLAS augmented RREF and extracts one particular solution through a single source-transparent native kernel. The kernel validates all shapes, detects inconsistent zero-left rows transactionally, and sets free variables to zero. Differential coverage includes underdetermined, overdetermined, singular, inconsistent, vector, multiple-RHS, and empty systems over GF(2), GF(7), and GF(97), plus native-disabled execution and inspectable isolated output. Warm 4-RHS medians for 120x180/180x120 fell from 672/677ms to 2.73/1.73ms over GF(2), 234/460ms to 1.55/1.51ms over GF(7), and 232/462ms to 1.45/1.36ms over GF(97).
risks: The complete pnpm test:native command reaches an unrelated pre-existing copied-byte Wasm expectation mismatch in test/ffi.cjs: the current declaration and lowered IR say wasm=true while the test still expects false.
architecture:packages requires an integration-owned linear-algebra bootstrap budget ratchet: actual size is 357586 bytes versus the current 354000-byte budget.
next_steps: At integration, ratchet the shared linear-algebra source budget to at least 357586 bytes with narrow headroom.
Resolve the base branch FlintByteRegion Wasm target expectation, then rerun pnpm test:native and mark this task review/complete.
